monarch.definition: Large migratory American butterfly having deep orange wings with black and white markings.
monarch.exampleUsage: The monarch laid an egg on a milkweed leaf.

swallowtail.definition: A butterfly of the swallowtail family, many species of which have tail-like extensions on the hindwings.
swallowtail.exampleUsage: The swallowtail rested with its hindwing extensions visible.

painted-lady.definition: A widespread orange, brown, black, and white butterfly species scientifically known as Vanessa cardui.
painted-lady.exampleUsage: A painted lady rested on a flower in the garden.

blue-morpho.definition: A large tropical butterfly known for its bright blue upper wings.
blue-morpho.exampleUsage: The blue morpho showed its blue upper wings during flight.

admiral.definition: A butterfly bearing the common name admiral, including species such as the red admiral.
admiral.exampleUsage: The red admiral fed on a garden flower.

cabbage-white.definition: A small white butterfly whose caterpillars often feed on cabbage plants.
cabbage-white.exampleUsage: The cabbage white laid eggs on a suitable host plant.

skipper.definition: A butterfly of a group commonly called skippers, often with a stout body and quick flight.
skipper.exampleUsage: The skipper flew quickly between the flowers.

fritillary.definition: A butterfly with the common name fritillary, many species of which have orange or brown wings with patterned spots.
fritillary.exampleUsage: The fritillary rested with its patterned wings open.

sulphur.definition: A butterfly of the group commonly called sulphurs, many of which have yellow or orange wings.
sulphur.exampleUsage: The sulphur butterfly visited the flower bed.

viceroy.definition: Showy American butterfly resembling the monarch but smaller.
viceroy.exampleUsage: The viceroy in the verified photograph has a dark line across the hindwing.

caterpillar.definition: A young insect that looks like a worm before becoming a butterfly or moth.
caterpillar.exampleUsage: The caterpillar fed on a host plant before pupation.

chrysalis.definition: The pupal stage of a butterfly, distinct from a silk cocoon that may surround some insects’ pupae.
chrysalis.exampleUsage: The adult emerged from the chrysalis.

butterfly.definition: An insect of the butterfly group, with scaled wings in its adult stage.
butterfly.exampleUsage: The butterfly rested on a flower with its wings closed.

metamorphosis.definition: The developmental transformation through egg, larva, pupa, and adult stages in butterflies.
metamorphosis.exampleUsage: The butterfly's metamorphosis includes larval and pupal stages.

molt.definition: The shedding of an arthropod’s old outer covering during growth.
molt.exampleUsage: The caterpillar's molt marks the transition to its next instar.

instar.definition: A developmental stage of an arthropod between molts.
instar.exampleUsage: The caterpillar grew during its final instar before pupation.

emerge.definition: To come out of the pupal casing as an adult butterfly.
emerge.exampleUsage: Adult butterflies emerge from their pupal casings.

wing-dry.definition: An inherited label for the stage when a newly emerged butterfly’s expanded wings dry and harden.
wing-dry.exampleUsage: The record uses the label wing dry for the period when expanded wings dry and harden.

first-flight.definition: The first time a young or newly emerged animal flies.
first-flight.exampleUsage: The observer recorded the butterfly's first flight after its wings hardened.

wing.definition: One of a butterfly’s thin body structures used for flight.
wing.exampleUsage: The butterfly folded a wing beside its body.

antenna.definition: One of the paired sensory appendages on an insect’s head.
antenna.exampleUsage: The butterfly moved an antenna while resting on the flower.

proboscis.definition: The elongated mouthpart used by many butterflies to take in liquids.
proboscis.exampleUsage: The butterfly uncoiled its proboscis to take in nectar.

thorax.definition: The middle region of the body of an arthropod between the head and the abdomen.
thorax.exampleUsage: The butterfly's legs attach to the thorax.

abdomen.definition: The rear body region of an insect, behind the thorax.
abdomen.exampleUsage: The abdomen lies behind the insect's thorax.

eye.definition: A sensory organ used for vision, typically a compound eye in an adult butterfly.
eye.exampleUsage: The close-up reference shows the butterfly's compound eye.

leg.definition: One of an adult insect’s six walking appendages, attached to its thorax.
leg.exampleUsage: One leg rested against the flower petal.

scale.definition: A tiny flattened structure covering a butterfly’s wings or body.
scale.exampleUsage: The magnified reference shows a tiny scale from the wing surface.

vein.definition: A reinforcing structure carrying tissues or fluids within an insect wing.
vein.exampleUsage: A vein supports the thin tissue of the wing.

spiracle.definition: A small opening on an insect's body through which it breathes.
spiracle.exampleUsage: Air enters the insect's breathing system through a spiracle.

milkweed.definition: Any of numerous plants of the genus Asclepias having milky juice and pods that split open releasing seeds with downy tufts.
milkweed.exampleUsage: The monarch caterpillar fed on a milkweed leaf.

lavender.definition: An aromatic flowering plant of the genus Lavandula.

zinnia.definition: Any of various plants of the genus Zinnia cultivated for their variously and brightly colored flower heads.
zinnia.exampleUsage: A butterfly landed on the brightly colored zinnia.

marigold.definition: Any of various tropical American plants of the genus Tagetes widely cultivated for their showy yellow or orange flowers.
marigold.exampleUsage: The marigold grew beside the garden path.

sunflower.definition: A tall plant with a large yellow flower and edible seeds.
sunflower.exampleUsage: The sunflower's broad flower head rose above the bed.

coneflower.definition: A plant commonly called coneflower, including Echinacea or Rudbeckia, with a prominent central flower-head cone.
coneflower.exampleUsage: The coneflower has a prominent central flower-head cone.

aster.definition: Any of various chiefly fall-blooming herbs of the genus Aster with showy daisylike flowers.
aster.exampleUsage: The aster flowered beside the late-season border.

lantana.definition: A flowering plant of the genus Lantana, commonly with clustered small flowers.
lantana.exampleUsage: The lantana carried clusters of small flowers.

verbena.definition: Any of numerous tropical or subtropical American plants of the genus Verbena grown for their showy spikes of variously colored flowers.
verbena.exampleUsage: The verbena produced flowers in the managed garden bed.

buddleia.definition: A flowering shrub commonly called butterfly bush, with clustered flowers; species and local planting suitability vary.
buddleia.exampleUsage: The buddleia shrub carried long clusters of flowers.

nectar-feeding.definition: Taking sweet liquid from flowers as a source of food.
nectar-feeding.exampleUsage: Nectar feeding continued while the butterfly remained on the flower.

basking.definition: Resting in sunlight to warm the body.
basking.exampleUsage: Basking in sunlight helped the butterfly warm its body.

mating.definition: The act of pairing a male and female for reproductive purposes.
mating.exampleUsage: The observer recorded mating behavior without disturbing the pair.

laying-eggs.definition: Depositing eggs so that young animals can develop.
laying-eggs.exampleUsage: The female was laying eggs on a suitable host plant.

migration.definition: The periodic passage of groups of animals (especially birds or fishes) from one region to another for feeding or breeding.
migration.exampleUsage: The tracking study records the monarch's seasonal migration.

camouflage.definition: Appearance or behavior that makes an organism less noticeable against its surroundings.
camouflage.exampleUsage: The resting insect's camouflage made it less conspicuous against the leaf.

mimicry.definition: Resembling another organism to gain protection or another advantage.
mimicry.exampleUsage: The guide compared the wing patterns as an example of mimicry.

puddling.definition: Butterflies gathering on damp ground to take in water and minerals.
puddling.exampleUsage: Several butterflies were puddling on the damp ground.

roosting.definition: Resting in a sheltered position, often overnight, in this butterfly context.
roosting.exampleUsage: Roosting butterflies remained in a sheltered position overnight.

territorial.definition: Displaying behavior associated with occupying or defending a particular area.
territorial.exampleUsage: The guide recorded territorial behavior around the occupied patch.

pathway.definition: A prepared route for visitors to walk through the garden.
pathway.exampleUsage: Visitors followed the pathway around the garden.

bench.definition: A long seat provided for garden visitors.
bench.exampleUsage: The visitor rested on the bench beside the fountain.

fountain.definition: A structure that sends water upward and lets it fall back down.
fountain.exampleUsage: Water flowed through the fountain in the courtyard.

trellis.definition: A supporting framework for climbing plants.
trellis.exampleUsage: The climbing plant grew across the trellis.

greenhouse.definition: A building with glass walls or a roof for growing plants.
greenhouse.exampleUsage: The greenhouse sheltered the plants from cold outdoor conditions.

sign.definition: A board showing rules or information.
sign.exampleUsage: The sign gave visitors information about the permitted route.

magnifying-glass.definition: A handheld tool uses a curved lens to make nearby details appear larger for close viewing or reading.
magnifying-glass.exampleUsage: The magnifying glass made the small surface details easier to see.

net.definition: A mesh tool or barrier used under the garden’s authorized arrangements.
net.exampleUsage: The authorized researcher carried a net for the permitted survey.

guide-book.definition: A book that helps identify species or gives information about a place.
guide-book.exampleUsage: The guide book helped the visitor compare recorded species features.

camera.definition: A device for recording photographs or moving images.
camera.exampleUsage: The visitor used a camera to photograph the garden from the path.
